# Kourovka Problem 8.28 (varieties generated by finitely based quasivarieties)

The proposition that for every finite set $Q$ of quasi-identities of groups, the variety generated by the quasivariety of groups satisfying $Q$ (with laws the words that hold in every such group) is finitely based. A quasi-identity is a sentence $\forall x\,(w_1 = 1 \wedge \dots \wedge w_k = 1 \to w = 1)$ with finitely many premises, all words in finitely many unknowns.

Source: E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 8.28 (A. V. Kuznetsov).
